title: Ternary Operator and Logical Operations
concept: Concise conditional expressions with the ternary operator (?:), and short-circuit evaluation with && and ||

steps.title: Starting main and initializing variables
steps.explanation: **`int age = 20;`** and **`int has_id = 1;`** -- Two integer variables are created in the stack frame. `age` is the age (20), and `has_id` indicates whether an ID is held (1 = yes).

steps.title: Conditional assignment with ternary operator
steps.explanation: **`char *status = (age >= 18) ? "Adult" : "Minor";`** -- The **ternary operator** compresses if-else into **a single line**.

steps.title: Printing status
steps.explanation: **`printf("Status: %s\n", status);`** -- `%s` is the string format specifier. It reads `"Adult"` that `status` points to and prints `Status: Adult`.

steps.title: && (Logical AND) - both conditions true
steps.explanation: **`if (age >= 18 && has_id) {`** -- The **`&&` (logical AND)** operator evaluates to true only when **both** conditions are true. `20 >= 18` (true) && `has_id` (1, true) -> true, so the if block executes.

steps.title: AND condition passed - entry allowed output
steps.explanation: **`printf("Entry allowed\n");`** -- Since both conditions are true, `"Entry allowed"` is printed. This expresses the requirement "must be at least 18 years old AND have an ID to enter" in code.

steps.title: || (Logical OR) short-circuit evaluation
steps.explanation: **`int result = (age > 0) || (10 / 0);`** -- `||` (logical OR) evaluates to true if **at least one** side is true. However, `(10 / 0)` is division by zero, which would **crash** the program if executed!

steps.title: Short-circuit result output and termination
steps.explanation: **`printf("Short-circuit: %d\n", result);`** -- `result = 1` is printed. Thanks to short-circuit evaluation, the division by zero was completely avoided.

quiz.explanation:
The || operator does not evaluate the right side if the left side is true (short-circuit evaluation).
Since x = 5, (x > 0) is true. Therefore func() is never called.
If x were -1, then (x > 0) would be false and func() would be executed.

misconceptions.correct: C's logical operators use short-circuit evaluation. Once the result is determined, the rest is ignored.
misconceptions.why: For &&, if the left side is false the entire expression is false; for ||, if the left side is true the entire expression is true -- so the result is already determined.

keyTakeaway: The ternary operator provides concise conditional expressions, and short-circuit evaluation with &&/|| skips unnecessary operations for safer code.
